summary:
All CONTRACT §8 audio is done and passes QA: 2 music loops, 3 ambience loops and 36 SFX, each as .ogg (Vorbis q4) plus .mp3, all at 44.1 kHz. SFX are mono; music and ambience are stereo. Total size is 5.56 MB (limit 8 MB). Everything is made by procedural synthesis, and two clean builds from scratch gave byte-identical files. I can't listen to audio, so every sound was judged from measurements, spectrograms, waveforms and Chromium decode tests. A person should listen before release.

Earlier work: the synthesis toolkit (synth.py, instruments.py, preview.py) was good, so I kept it. Its tuning is within 1 cent. The music generator fa_music.py was musically sound, so I kept it as music.py and fixed two things:
- A real click at the loop start: notes humanised to before t=0 had their attacks cut off. Its second-difference (d2) ratio at the wrap was 1.08, now 0.07.
- A slightly brighter master EQ.

**bgm_village** (100 bpm, 76.8 s):
- F major, 32 bars in A1 A2 B A3 form.
- Pentatonic hook "A C D – C A C –" over F | Dm | Bb | C (A section), with a B section of Bb C Am Dm … Gm7 C7.
- Marimba lead, ocarina in B, music-box and glockenspiel doubling, swung off-beat plucks, pizzicato bass, kick on 1 and 3, brushed snare, shaker and sleigh bells.

**bgm_title**: 84 bpm, 22.9 s, music-box version of the hook with harp arpeggios.

**New scripts:**
- ambience.py: wind gusts with a soft howl, sea waves (swell, soft break, foam fizz) every ~6 s, and a campfire with roar plus crackles and snaps.
- sfx.py: all 36 SFX, layered transient + body + texture, with a per-key "punch" limiter so they read on phone speakers. Musical SFX are in F major. sfx_pickup is a pop settling on C5 (measured −1.9 cents). sfx_complete quotes the village hook as a brass/glockenspiel fanfare.
- build_audio.py: render, encode, measure with ffmpeg ebur128, write the manifest and the listening page.
- check_audio.py: QA.
- demo_mix.py: renders a 30 s gameplay mix.
- ffmpeg_tools.py and deps.py: helpers.

**Found and fixed: OGG loops would glitch in Chrome.** Chromium's decodeAudioData ignores the Vorbis end-trim and was appending 32–960 samples (up to 22 ms) of codec padding to every OGG loop. I confirmed this in headless Chromium 141. The build now sets each loop's length to the nearest Vorbis block boundary:
- Music: the same performance, with the loop point moved: bgm_village −64 samples (1.5 ms), bgm_title +320 samples (7 ms).
- Ambience: re-rendered at lengths ≤ 48 samples longer.

All five loops now decode sample-exact in Chromium for both OGG and MP3, and the OGG wraps are click-free (wrap ratios 0.05–0.9).

**Mix:** files are mastered loud (SFX peak −1.5 dBFS, music −18 LUFS, ambience −20/−21 LUFS), and the manifest volume brings each to its target. At the volumes the game code actually passes, hero SFX sit about 7 dB above the music+ambience bed, footsteps and station sounds sit just under it, and the busiest scripted moment peaks at −0.9 dBFS.

QA results: every decoded file has sample peak ≤ −1.1 dBFS, DC under 0.001, no leading silence, and RESULT: OK. I saw no unexpected changes in my folders. I did not touch src/, bl_common.py or pack_utils.py, and ran no state-changing git commands.
contract_gaps: None missing: all 41 §8 keys exist with [ogg, mp3], and the 4 audioGroups match the contract exactly (check_audio.py verifies this against its own copy of §8).

Extra manifest fields (allowed by 'new keys are fine'): top-level 'generator'; per key 'duration' (exact seconds); loops also have 'loopSamples' and 'mp3StartPad' (1105); music has 'bpm' and 'bars'; sfx_pickup has 'pitch': 'C5' and 'pitchHz': 523.25.

Loop lengths differ slightly from nominal so they land on Vorbis block boundaries: bgm_village 3386816 samples (76.7985 s, 64 samples short of 32 bars at 100 bpm, so the downbeat after the wrap is 1.5 ms early); bgm_title 1008320 (+7 ms); amb_wind and amb_sea 1058432; amb_fire 882048.
sfx_saw, sfx_smelt, sfx_sizzle and sfx_oven are one-shots (0.8–0.9 s, loop:false, kind sfx), matching how Station.js plays them (once per processed item, 400 ms throttle). They are not machine loops.
On-disk OGGs for very short SFX decode about 20 ms longer than the true length because of codec padding (silent). This is harmless for one-shots; manifest 'duration' is the true length.
regenerate: cd /home/user/nurient/frost-village && python3 tools/audio/build_audio.py   (~70 s on 3 cores: renders into tools/audio/_cache, fits loops to Vorbis block boundaries, encodes .ogg+.mp3 into assets/audio, writes manifest.json and docs/previews/audio_preview.html, then runs check_audio.py; exit code 1 on any failure). Options: --only sfx_coin,amb_sea | --skip-render (re-encode and re-balance only, e.g. after editing SOUNDS targets or HEADROOM_DB in build_audio.py) | --no-check. Optional: python3 tools/audio/demo_mix.py (30 s gameplay mix preview). Needs numpy + scipy + Pillow + ffmpeg. System python3 has no scipy, so deps.py automatically re-runs the script with /tmp/fv_audio_venv/bin/python; on another PC run: pip install numpy scipy pillow.
notes_for_integrator:
1) MANIFEST AND VOLUMES. assets/audio/manifest.json is a standard §2 fragment that Assets.js already reads. The 'volume' field is the base gain; Audio.js multiplies it by the call-site volume. Volumes are loudness-normalised to targets set in SOUNDS in build_audio.py:
- music: integrated −24.5 LUFS (village) / −23.5 (title)
- ambience: −31 to −32.5
- sfx: max momentary loudness −14 (sfx_complete) to −20 (sfx_pad_fill)
- plus a global HEADROOM_DB = −2 because WebAudio sums sources and hard-clips at 0 dBFS.
Final volumes: bgm_village 0.376, bgm_title 0.422, amb_wind 0.193, amb_sea 0.216, amb_fire 0.257; chop 0.85–0.90, mine ~0.71, harvest ~0.53, splash 0.407, reel 0.501, bow 0.596, hit_animal 0.661, deer 0.285, boar 0.473, pickup 0.617, drop 0.776, coin 0.447, coins_many 0.473, cash 0.372, unlock 0.412, build 0.49, levelup 0.389, hire 0.525, click 0.977, error 0.266, whoosh 0.422, step_snow 0.79–0.94, saw 0.282, smelt 0.403, sizzle 0.292, oven 0.299, customer_happy 0.422, pad_fill 0.933, complete 0.519.
With the call-site volumes currently in src/ the hierarchy works: hero SFX about +7 dB over the music bed, footsteps (×0.32) and station sounds (×0.45) just under it. For the player's own item pickup (not yet in src/), I suggest Audio.play('sfx_pickup', {volume: 0.6–1, rate: 1 + n*0.08}). sfx_pickup's settled pitch is C5, so rate r gives C5 × r. If you want a louder overall game, add a WebAudio DynamicsCompressor/limiter on the Phaser master output and set HEADROOM_DB to 0.

2) LOOPS. Phaser loops by re-scheduling a source for the full buffer.duration, so the decoded buffer must be exactly the loop. Chromium's decodeAudioData ignores the Vorbis end-trim (verified in headless Chromium 141), so the build places every loop on a Vorbis block boundary: OGG end padding is 0, and check_audio.py fails the build if it is not. In Chromium both OGG and MP3 decode to exactly loopSamples.
- MP3 is the fallback mainly for iOS Safari, which I could not test. The MP3s carry LAME gapless info (delay 576 + 529 decoder delay).
- If a browser ignores that info, the decoded buffer will be longer than loopSamples. Fix: when buffer.length > loopSamples, loop a Phaser marker {start: mp3StartPad/44100, duration: loopSamples/44100}. This is optional robustness and needs a game-code change.
- MP3 wrap discontinuity metrics are slightly higher than OGG for amb_wind (1.84) and bgm_title (1.04). That is noise-like codec error at the edge, not a transient.

3) PREVIEWS for humans:
- docs/previews/audio_preview.html: a listening page that plays every sound at its manifest volume via WebAudio, with sample-accurate loops and a 'mix test'. Open it through the game's static server, not file://. Tested in Chromium at 390 px width: no errors, no horizontal scroll.
- docs/previews/audio_mix_demo.ogg/.mp3: a 30 s scripted gameplay soundscape at the real call-site volumes.
- docs/previews/audio_waveforms.png, audio_spectrograms.png and audio_report.txt: full QA table (duration, sample/true peak, I/Mmax LUFS, DC, size, loop metrics).

4) OTHER.
- Ambience is meant to be driven by Audio.setAmbience(key, 0..1) proximity; the base volumes already sit well under the music.
- sfx_error is a soft two-note 'nuh-uh'; sfx_customer_happy is a synthesized cute 'yay!' plus music-box sparkle (the riskiest design, worth a human listen); sfx_complete is about 4.15 s.
- tools/audio/_cache is gitignored; I deleted fa_music.py (it was tracked; now music.py). synth.py only had a docstring fix; instruments.py and preview.py are unchanged.
- No unexpected file changes were seen in my folders during the session.
